newsitem.title: USA: Madison Ave. group head quits in Puerto Rico flap.
newsitem.headline: Madison Ave. group head quits in Puerto Rico flap.

text.p: The head of a business group criticised for urging members to close down during the Puerto Rico Day parade scheduled for Sunday resigned Thursday, the group said.
A spokeswoman for the Madison Avenue Business Improvement District (BID) said the group had accepted the resignation of president Alexander Kabbaz.
He said he had acted without the consent of his executive committee in issuing the warning about the parade near Madison Avenue's exclusive boutiques and shops.
The annual event is a showcase for New York's 900,000 residents of Puerto Rican ancestry and draws huge crowds. It runs down Fifth Avenue, a block from Madison Avenue.

Kabbaz oversaw the distribution of leaflets to storekeepers reading: "We would advise that your establishment remain shut this Sunday ... (and) the removal of expensive merchandise from your windows." The flyers also referred to the parade date as a "difficult day."

Mayor Rudy Giuliani, who will be marching in the parade, said Kabbaz's remarks were "really quite ignorant." Giuliani visited stores along Madison Avenue Thursday, rallying owners to keep their doors open on.
Giuliani said the city expected to generate $43 million in sales as a result of the parade and stores along Madison Avenue could take in as much as $3 million.
City officials expect between 2.5 million and 3 million spectators at Sunday's parade.
"This isn't the spirit of New York," said Bronx Borough President Fernando Ferrer, himself of Puerto Rican ancestry, when he heard about the flyers.
The executive committee of the Madison Avenue group said they would distribute their own pamphlets asking store owners to stay open for business.
"Parades are one of the true treasures of this city," the panel said in a statement.
A spokeswoman for the association said the leaflet arose from concerns about the beating death of a young man near Madison Avenue during St. Patrick's Day parade in March.
